claims.text: Tribo-corrosion in high-entropy alloys is governed by the balance between friction-induced passive-film removal and electrochemically driven film reformation.
The protective surface film consists predominantly of Cr2O3 and Al2O3.
Wear that removes the passive film faster than it reforms causes localized exposure of the active substrate.
Localized substrate exposure promotes pitting corrosion.
Pitting corrosion weakens the material and amplifies mechanical damage, producing synergistic degradation.
Increasing Cr and Al content will accelerate and strengthen passive-oxide formation.
The enhanced-passivation alloy can reform its oxide film rapidly between successive wear events.
Rapid oxide reformation mitigates corrosion-assisted damage under moderate wear conditions.
An intermediate wear regime marks the transition at which film removal begins to overwhelm film restoration.
At intermediate or high mechanical wear, passive-film regeneration cannot keep pace with film removal.
At moderate to intermediate wear, the enhanced-passivation variant will have lower total degradation than the baseline alloy.
At moderate to intermediate wear, the enhanced-passivation variant will show reduced wear depth, weight loss, and anodic current density relative to the baseline.
In wear-only tests, the baseline and modified alloys will exhibit similar mechanical wear.
Similar wear-only behavior combined with different tribo-corrosion behavior would show that the modified alloy's benefit arises from the corrosion component.
At extreme loads, the benefit of passive-film reformation will be negated and the two alloys will approach similar degradation levels.
The comparison will use sliding tests in 3.5 wt% NaCl and parallel wear-only tests in a non-corrosive or inert environment.
Passive-film reformation rate, wear depth, weight loss, anodic current density, and pitting can be measured across varying loads to test the proposed mechanism.
The load threshold at which passive-film reformation fails is not known and requires empirical determination.

contradictions.description: The baseline is specified as equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi and therefore contains no stated Al, yet the passive film is described generally as predominantly including Al2O3. Al2O3 formation is not compositionally coherent for the stated baseline without an external Al source.

Both variants are introduced as equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi, but the modified variant has enhanced Cr and added or enhanced Al. Such a variant cannot remain the stated equiatomic five-element composition unless its full revised composition is separately defined.

The conditions call for identical contact pressures while also stating that the wear regimes will be created by adjusting load/contact pressure. Contact pressure cannot simultaneously be identical and varied across those regimes without clarifying which comparisons are held matched.

The intermediate regime is inconsistently assigned: it is described both as the point where restoration is overwhelmed and as a regime where the enhanced alloy retains lower degradation and effective film regeneration. A narrower transition definition is needed.
